question.text: SEBI (AIF) Regulations prescribe NAV disclosure frequency for Category III AIFs. What is the correct disclosure frequency?

answer.text: Monthly for closed-ended Cat III; quarterly for open-ended Cat III
Daily for both open and closed-ended Cat III
Quarterly for closed-ended Cat III; monthly for open-ended Cat III
Half-yearly for closed-ended Cat III; monthly for open-ended Cat III

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 14.10 and Section 14.14, NAV on each Valuation Day is disclosed to investors QUARTERLY for closed-ended Cat III AIFs and MONTHLY for open-ended Cat III AIFs. Daily NAV is an operational practice (especially for listed-only funds) but not the mandated disclosure frequency. The Trap: Option A swaps the two frequencies. Option B confuses valuation-day with disclosure frequency. Half-yearly is the Cat I/II valuer cycle. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests this at high frequency. XIX-C asks you to MANAGE the calendar — valuation day, accounting lag, and disclosure deadline are three distinct items. Manager's Pro-Tip: Set a T+15 internal deadline between valuation day and investor NAV disclosure. Many Cat III funds miss quarterly windows because the independent valuer for unlisted sleeves runs late — keep a calendar chase on the valuer.
